explain.say: If an animal comes closer, the skunk stamps, hisses and raises its tail. Spotted skunks even do a handstand. Then it bends into a U shape so both its eyes and its tail face the enemy.

faq.q: Why are skunks black and white?
faq.a: Bold black and white is warning colouring. It is easy to see even at night, and predators that have been sprayed once remember it and keep away, so the skunk rarely needs to spray.
asks: What does a skunk's colour mean?

faq.q: How does a skunk aim its spray?
faq.a: It twists its body into a U shape, so its head and its raised tail both point at the enemy. Muscles around the two glands can send a fine mist or a direct stream, and it can aim at the face from about 3 metres.
asks: How far can a skunk spray?

faq.q: Why does skunk spray smell so bad?
faq.a: The spray contains thiols, sulfur chemicals like those in rotten eggs and garlic, and our noses detect them in tiny amounts. It also has chemicals that turn into more thiols when wet, so a sprayed dog smells again after a bath.
asks: What is skunk spray made of?
Why does skunk smell come back when wet?

faq.q: Can a skunk run out of spray?
faq.a: Yes. A skunk carries enough for about five or six sprays, and it takes around ten days to refill its glands, which is why it warns first and sprays only as a last resort.
asks: How many times can a skunk spray?
Why do skunks warn before spraying?

faq.q: Does tomato juice get rid of skunk smell?
faq.a: Not really; it mostly masks the smell. A mix of hydrogen peroxide, baking soda and a little dish soap works better, because it breaks down the thiols. Keep it away from the eyes.
asks: How do you clean skunk spray off a dog?

facts: Skunk spray gets its smell mainly from thiols, sulfur-containing chemicals.
A skunk can spray about five or six times before it needs around ten days to refill its glands.

quiz.why: With only about five sprays at a time and days to refill, warning saves its ammunition.
